disposal_consumer: The Act sets a target of deciding a complaint within 3 months — or 5 months if the goods need laboratory testing.
fee_rule: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020, as amended August 2023. The fee is fixed by the value of the goods or services you paid as consideration — not by the compensation you claim.

limitation_consumer: A complaint must be filed within 2 years of the date the cause of action arose (Section 69, Consumer Protection Act, 2019). Filed late, it is time-barred unless you ask for condonation and satisfy the Commission of sufficient cause.

scenarios.desc: You returned a product or cancelled an order, the refund never came, and support keeps saying “wait 24–48 hours”. File with the NCH first, then the Consumer Commission.
documents: Payment proof (UPI / bank statement / card slip)
Return pickup proof or cancellation confirmation
Screenshots of chats and emails with support
Your written complaint to the platform and any reply

faq.a: Within 2 years of the date the problem arose (Section 69, Consumer Protection Act, 2019). The clock usually starts when the refund was due and not paid.
faq.q: How long do I have to file?

faq.a: No. You can file on e-Jagriti yourself as a party-in-person. The fee is nil if what you paid is up to ₹5 lakh.

It depends on what you paid as consideration, not the compensation you claim: up to ₹50 lakh — District Commission; above ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore — State Commission; above ₹2 crore — National Commission.

scenarios.keywords: flipkart refund complaint, amazon refund not received, meesho refund complaint, e-commerce refund
scenarios.relief: Full refund of the amount paid, compensation for harassment and mental agony, and the cost of filing.
steps: Write to the platform once more in the app or by email and keep a screenshot — the Commission wants proof you tried.
Register the grievance with the National Consumer Helpline — call 1915 or file at consumerhelpline.gov.in. Keep the docket number. Many refunds are settled here within about 30 days.
If the NCH route fails, file a consumer complaint on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in). The forum depends on what you paid: up to ₹50 lakh goes to the District Commission.
Pay the fee on the portal — nil if what you paid is up to ₹5 lakh.
Upload the complaint, the notarised affidavit, the order/invoice, payment proof, return proof and your messages with the platform, all as PDFs.
Track the case on your e-Jagriti dashboard. The opposite party must file its version within 30 days (extendable by 15).
scenarios.title: Flipkart / Amazon / Meesho refund complaint
scenarios.what: Refund not received after a return or cancellation on an e-commerce platform (Flipkart, Amazon, Meesho and others).

scenarios.desc: The product arrived damaged, stopped working in days, or is not what was promised. The seller refuses a replacement or refund. This is the classic consumer complaint.
documents: Photos or video of the defect
Written complaint to the seller and any reply

faq.a: A warranty cannot override your rights under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. If the product was defective at delivery or failed unreasonably early, that is a deficiency in service / defective goods regardless of what the warranty card says.
faq.q: What if the seller says the warranty does not cover it?

faq.a: Yes. If the defect needs testing, the Commission sends the goods to a lab. The disposal target then becomes 5 months instead of 3.
faq.q: Can the Commission order a lab test?

scenarios.keywords: defective product complaint, damaged product refund, product not working consumer court
scenarios.relief: Replacement of the product, or a full refund; compensation for loss and harassment; litigation costs.
steps: Photograph or video the defect before you use the product further, and keep the original packing.
Complain to the seller in writing (email or app) and keep the reply or the lack of one.
Register with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in) — many sellers settle once the NCH forwards the grievance.
If it is not resolved, file on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in) with the forum picked by what you paid.
Upload the complaint, affidavit, bill, warranty card, photos/videos of the defect and all correspondence as PDFs.
The Commission may order a lab test of the goods — in that case the disposal target is 5 months instead of 3.
scenarios.title: Defective product complaint
scenarios.what: A product that is defective, damaged, spurious, or not as described — and the seller or manufacturer will not replace it or refund you.

scenarios.desc: You paid in full, the order shows “out for delivery” for days or was marked delivered when nothing arrived, and the seller will not refund you.
documents: Complaint to the seller/platform and any reply

faq.a: Screenshot the tracking page, ask the delivery partner for proof of delivery in writing, and keep both. A false delivery scan is strong evidence of deficiency in service.
faq.q: The tracking says “delivered” but I got nothing. What do I do?

faq.a: No. Your contract is with the seller, not the courier. The seller is responsible for delivery.
faq.q: The seller says it will “check with the courier” forever. Is that a defence?

scenarios.keywords: order not delivered complaint, paid but not received, fake delivery complaint
scenarios.relief: Full refund of the amount paid, compensation for harassment, and the cost of filing.
steps: Take screenshots of the order status, the tracking page and the delivery confirmation (or lack of it).
Raise it with the seller/platform in writing and keep the ticket number.
Register the grievance with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in).
If unresolved, file on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in). The forum is picked by what you paid.
Upload the complaint, affidavit, invoice, payment proof and the order/tracking screenshots as PDFs.
scenarios.title: Order paid but never delivered
scenarios.what: Goods paid for but never delivered — or marked delivered when they were not.

scenarios.desc: The possession date in your agreement has passed and the builder keeps pushing it. Under RERA you can stay and claim interest for the delay, or withdraw and take a refund with interest.
documents: Agreement for sale (with the promised possession date)
Letters / emails to the builder demanding possession
Any revised possession letters from the builder

faq.a: Refund, interest or possession go to the RERA Authority (Section 31, usually Form M). Compensation for loss — beyond interest — goes to the Adjudicating Officer (Section 71, usually Form N). Many homebuyers file both.
faq.q: Should I file with the RERA Authority or the Adjudicating Officer?

faq.a: Typically SBI MCLR + 2% per year. State rules differ — for example, Uttar Pradesh links it to SBI MCLR + 1%. Your state portal shows the rate it applies.
Generally 3 years from the cause of action (Limitation Act, Article 137, as applied by the courts). The RERA Act itself does not fix a period — file sooner rather than later.

scenarios.keywords: delayed possession RERA complaint, builder delay flat, MahaRERA delayed possession, RERA interest delay
scenarios.relief: Possession with interest for the delay, or withdrawal with a full refund plus interest (typically SBI MCLR + 2% per year; state rules differ). Compensation is decided separately by the Adjudicating Officer.
steps: Check that the project is RERA-registered on your state RERA portal — this route only exists for registered projects.
Write to the builder demanding possession or a revised date, and keep the reply.
Decide what you want: stay and claim interest for the delay, or withdraw and claim a full refund with interest (Section 18).
File with the RERA Authority on your state portal — Form M in most states (Form A in Maharashtra). Fee ₹1,000 in most states, ₹5,000 in Maharashtra.
If you also want compensation beyond interest or refund, file separately with the Adjudicating Officer (Form N, usually ₹5,000).
The Authority's disposal target is 60 days. Either side can appeal to the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal within 60 days of the order.
scenarios.title: Builder delayed flat possession — RERA complaint
scenarios.what: A promoter who fails to hand over possession by the date agreed in the agreement for sale.

scenarios.desc: The project is stalled or the delay is so long that you want out. Under Section 18 of the RERA Act you can withdraw and get your full payment back with interest.
documents: All payment receipts and bank statements
Written refund demand to the builder with proof of delivery
Project status from the RERA portal

faq.a: Not under Section 18. If you withdraw because the promoter failed to complete or hand over possession on time, you are entitled to the entire amount paid, with interest.
faq.q: Can the builder deduct anything from my refund?

faq.a: The amount is recoverable as arrears of land revenue under Section 40 of the RERA Act.
faq.q: What if the builder ignores the RERA order?

scenarios.keywords: RERA refund complaint, withdraw from project refund, builder refund RERA Section 18
scenarios.relief: Full refund of everything you paid, with interest (typically SBI MCLR + 2% per year). Compensation, if claimed, is decided by the Adjudicating Officer.
steps: Confirm the project is RERA-registered on your state portal.
Send the builder a written demand for a refund, citing the delay and Section 18, and keep proof of delivery.
File with the RERA Authority on your state portal (Form M in most states; Form A in Maharashtra). Fee ₹1,000 in most states, ₹5,000 in Maharashtra.
If you also want compensation for your loss (beyond interest), file with the Adjudicating Officer (Form N, usually ₹5,000).
Attend the hearing with your payment records. The Authority's disposal target is 60 days.
If the builder does not comply with the order, it is recoverable as arrears of land revenue (Section 40).
scenarios.title: Builder refund — withdraw from the project
scenarios.what: Withdrawing from a stalled or endlessly delayed project and claiming a full refund with interest under Section 18 of the RERA Act, 2016.

scenarios.desc: Your flight was cancelled or heavily delayed, the airline offered a voucher instead of a refund, or the refund never arrived. Airlines must refund to the original payment method.
documents: Cancellation or delay notice from the airline
Written refund request and the airline's reply

faq.a: No. If the airline cancels the flight, you are entitled to a refund to the original payment method. A voucher is only acceptable if you agree to it.
faq.q: Can the airline force me to take a voucher?

faq.a: It depends on what you paid for the ticket: up to ₹50 lakh — District Commission; above ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore — State Commission; above ₹2 crore — National Commission. Almost every individual ticket lands in the District Commission, and the fee is nil up to ₹5 lakh.

scenarios.keywords: airline refund complaint, flight cancelled refund, DGCA refund complaint, airline voucher instead of refund
scenarios.relief: Full refund to the original payment method, compensation for the loss caused by the cancellation, and the cost of filing.
steps: Keep the booking, the cancellation message and any voucher the airline offered.
Complain to the airline in writing and ask for a refund to the original payment method, not a voucher.
Register the grievance with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in).
If unresolved, file on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in). The forum is picked by what you paid for the ticket.
Upload the complaint, affidavit, ticket, payment proof, cancellation notice and correspondence as PDFs.
scenarios.title: Flight cancelled — airline refund complaint
scenarios.what: A cancelled or significantly delayed flight where the airline refuses a refund to the original payment method, or delays it beyond a reasonable time.

scenarios.desc: Your bill has charges you never agreed to, a plan was changed without consent, or the connection keeps failing and the provider will not fix it or refund you.
documents: The plan / tariff you agreed to
Complaint to the provider and appellate authority, with reference numbers
Speed-test logs or outage records (for service deficiency)

faq.a: It is not a legal precondition for the Consumer Commission, but the Commission expects you to have tried. A written complaint with a reference number strengthens your case.
faq.q: Do I have to go to the provider's appellate authority first?

faq.a: The fee is nil for claims up to ₹5 lakh, so a small claim costs nothing to file. Small claims are exactly what the District Commission is for.
faq.q: What if the amount is small, like ₹500?

scenarios.keywords: wrong mobile bill complaint, broadband bill dispute, telecom complaint consumer court, TRAI complaint
scenarios.relief: Correction of the bill and refund of excess charges, compensation for deficient service, and the cost of filing.
steps: Keep the bills, the plan details you agreed to, and screenshots of the wrong charges.
Complain to the provider's appellate authority in writing (every provider must have one) and keep the reference number.
Register the grievance with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in).
If unresolved, file on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in). The forum is picked by what you paid.
Upload the complaint, affidavit, bills, plan details, speed-test or outage records and correspondence as PDFs.
scenarios.title: Wrong mobile / broadband bill complaint
scenarios.what: Incorrect billing, unauthorised charges, or a deficient telecom/broadband service.

scenarios.desc: The hospital charged for medicines or tests you never received, inflated the bill, or refused an itemised bill. You can challenge the bill before the Consumer Commission.
documents: Written request for an itemised bill and the hospital's reply

faq.a: Yes. Medical services are covered, and billing disputes and deficiency in service can be taken to the Consumer Commission.
faq.q: Is a hospital a “service provider” under the Consumer Protection Act?

faq.a: Paying does not waive your rights. Keep the payment proof and the itemised bill — you can still claim a refund of the excess.
faq.q: What if I already paid the full bill under pressure?

scenarios.keywords: hospital overbilling complaint, hospital bill dispute consumer court, medical bill complaint India
scenarios.relief: Refund of the excess charges, compensation for the deficiency, and the cost of filing.
steps: Demand an itemised bill in writing and keep the request and the bill you received.
Mark every charge you dispute and collect proof — prescriptions, test reports, discharge summary.
Register the grievance with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in).
If unresolved, file on e-Jagriti (e-jagriti.gov.in). The forum is picked by what you paid.
Upload the complaint, affidavit, itemised bill, discharge summary, prescriptions and correspondence as PDFs.
scenarios.title: Hospital overbilling complaint
scenarios.what: A hospital bill that charges for services, medicines or tests not provided, or prices far above what was agreed or reasonable.
